lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: reflecting without shame

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 6 — family contribution capstone
objective: Learners write a private reflection on their family helper job using three specific prompts — one thing that went as planned, one thing to do differently next time, and one skill from this unit (choosing, listing, safety-checking, doing, or checking) they feel most confident using again — treating any forgotten step or rough moment as useful planning information rather than something to feel bad about.
scenario: In a private space, the learner writes or draws answers to the three reflection prompts about their own completed helper job, without a guardian reading the specific content. Afterward, the learner tells the guardian only that the reflection is finished, and the guardian confirms the reflection happened and asks the learner to name, out loud, which one of the three prompts felt most useful to think about, without asking to see the private writing itself.
safetyNotes: No heat, sharp tools, or chemical cleaners are used during this lesson; it is a private written or drawn reflection.

The guardian does not read or require disclosure of the learner's private written reflection; guardian confirmation covers only that the reflection was completed and which prompt the learner found most useful, not its content.

simulationAlternative.description: If the private reflection moment did not happen right after the job because time or a private space was not available, the learner instead completes a short written or drawn walkthrough of how the reflection would go, covering the same three prompts, and the guardian confirms afterward, as discussed together, that the walkthrough happened.

tasks.directions: Before writing, sit quietly for a moment and picture the whole job from start to finish, step by step.

prompts.text: Name one moment from the job, big or small, that you remember clearly right now.

tasks.directions: Write your private reflection using all three prompts, checking off each part as you finish it. No one else needs to read what you write unless you choose to share it.

prompts.text: I wrote about one specific thing that went as planned, naming the exact part, not just 'it went fine.'
I wrote about one specific thing to do differently next time, describing it as useful information for next time, not as a mistake to feel bad about.
I named one specific skill from this unit (choosing, listing, safety-checking, doing, or checking) that I feel most confident using again.
I kept my full written reflection private, sharing only that it is finished.

tasks.directions: Tell your guardian, out loud, that your reflection is finished, and name which one of the three prompts felt most useful to think about, without reading them your full private reflection.

prompts.text: Write down which of the three prompts (what went as planned, what you'd do differently, or the skill you feel confident in) you told your guardian was most useful, and why that one stood out.

tasks.directions: Look back at the 'do differently next time' part of your private reflection one more time.

prompts.text: Rewrite that one 'do differently' idea as a specific plan for next time, naming exactly what you would change, the same way useful information turns into a better next step rather than something to apologize for.

remediation: If a learner's 'do differently' answer uses judgment words about themselves, such as careless, lazy, or bad at this, instead of describing the specific step or moment, reteach by having them rewrite the sentence starting with 'Next time, I will...' followed only by the concrete action, with no words describing themselves at all.
extension: Have the learner write one sentence of encouragement they would give a friend who forgot the same step they did, then compare that sentence to how they first described their own moment, noticing any difference in tone.
